 Peak hours and evenings
 Several phones ringing, one person to answer them 
 1 One call at a time
 Your receptionist can handle one call at a time. Peak hours and evenings go to voicemail, and fee earners lose time chasing ID and signed forms.
 2 First to respond
 Someone with a legal problem calls several firms. The first to respond is usually the firm that gets instructed, and chased paperwork delays the fee.
 3 What comes back to you
 Overflow and evening calls answered and logged, with reminders and chasers added if you want them, on a schedule you set, and a written summary for each one.
 Options, not promises
 Tasks an agent can take on 
 Each of these can be scoped for your firm. What an agent will actually do for you is confirmed and written down before anything goes live, so read this as a menu.
 Overflow calls
 Can be scoped to pick up when the main line is busy, take the caller's details and leave a written summary for the right person.
 Out-of-hours calls
 An agent could be scoped to answer in the evening or at weekends, say when the office reopens and log what the caller wanted.
 Appointment confirmation
 Where outbound calling suits the firm, this could be scoped to ring ahead on a schedule you set and note anyone needing to rearrange.
 Document chasers
 A chaser could be scoped to remind clients about outstanding ID or signed forms and record the reply. It would never discuss what a document means.
 Fees
 A published starting point, scoped around your firm 
 Setup begins at £497, with monthly fees from £97. A firm wanting several tasks will pay more than one wanting overflow cover alone, and you see that figure in the written scope before committing.

 How a build runs
 Scoped first, scripted with the firm 
 01 Choose the tasks
 Tell Andy where calls are being lost and which chasers eat the most time. Together you decide what an agent should take on, if anything.
 02 Approve the script
 The firm reads and agrees every line, including how callers are told it is an AI and the point at which it must stop.
 03 Test and switch on
 Your team rings it and tries to catch it out. Live calls only reach it once you are satisfied.

 Questions from partners
 What a firm will want settled before launch 
 Does it give legal advice?
 No, it never does. When a caller asks what they should do, it takes their details and tells them someone from the firm will respond.
 Who is responsible for what it says?
 The firm remains responsible. The script is agreed with you before launch, later changes go through you as well, and checking it against your professional duties is a job for the firm.
 How is confidentiality handled?
 An agent is given only what the scoped task requires, and summaries go only to the people you name. Where data is held, how long it is kept and which software it connects to are all confirmed and written into your scope before anything goes live.
 Can it run conflict checks?
 No. It collects the details and your team runs that check.
 Is it different from a legal answering service?
 A legal answering service or law firm answering service generally takes a message. An agent can be scoped to act on a schedule too, such as confirming appointments or chasing documents. For front-desk cover on its own, see our sister site on answering calls for solicitors .
 Can it deal with new enquiries?
 Some firms call this AI legal intake. An agent can be scoped to note the basic facts and pass them on, but it never decides whether the firm takes the matter.
 Is a caller told they are speaking to software?
 Yes. The agent tells them early in the call, using wording the firm has approved.
 Cover the calls that are reaching voicemail.

## https://aivoiceagentsforlawfirms.co.uk/about-andy

Who builds your agent
 Andy Norman, scoping voice agents for small firms 
 Before Antek Automation, Andy worked as a field engineer and then a service manager, spending more than three decades in field service and managed print.
 That background is operational, not legal. He looks at where a call goes unanswered or a chaser goes unmade, and at whether a voice agent is a sensible fix.
 What he will not do
 He will not tell you what your obligations are, and he will not write a script the firm has not approved. Responsibility for the words stays with the firm.
